item.title: Four Prentiss County schools will share one tennis region after spring 2027
item.description: Jumpertown and New Site will join Thrasher and Wheeler in the same high school tennis region under the Mississippi High School Activities Association’s 2027–29 assignments. The four Prentiss County schools account for four of the five places in Class I Region 1. Biggersville, in Alcorn County, has the fifth. The change will put six different pairings of those four county schools inside one region. Currently just two of those six pairings are within the same region. Jumpertown and New Site stay together in the change. For spring 2027, their Class I Region 2 also includes Baldwyn, Okolona and Tupelo Christian. All three of those opponents remain in Region 2 for the following cycle. The new Region 2 also includes Aberdeen and Bruce. The new Region 1 instead gives Jumpertown and New Site three other opponents in addition to one another. They are Biggersville, Thrasher and Wheeler. Thrasher and Wheeler are already in Class I Region 1 with Biggersville and Walnut. In the next cycle, Thrasher and Wheeler each keep two familiar opponents, gain two new ones and lose Walnut from the group. Instead of facing one another as their only county pairing within that region, the two schools will share it with both Jumpertown and New Site. The distinction matters for the upcoming spring team tournament. Under the published 2026–27 draw, a qualifier from Thrasher and Wheeler’s Region 1 faces a Region 4 opponent in the opening round. A qualifier from Jumpertown and New Site’s Region 2 faces a Region 3 opponent. In both pairings, the region champion opens against the other region’s fourth seed, and the runner-up opens against its third seed. The four county schools still have to earn their places. Booneville’s team follows a separate path. It finishes the current cycle in Class 3A Region 1 with Aberdeen, Alcorn Central, Belmont, Kossuth and Nettleton. In the next alignment the Blue Devils go into Class 4A Region 1 with Corinth, Itawamba Agricultural, Mooreville and Tishomingo County. The association has released region memberships and the coming spring’s playoff pairings. Match dates and venues are separate details. The association’s November 4 release is at https://www.misshsaa.com/2026/11/04/2027-29-tennis-regions/ . New assignment table: https://championship-manager-seven.vercel.app/api/embed/e3ee83d5a06539cbe6c2e8416fd1c84d . Current regions: https://www.misshsaa.com/2024/11/20/2025-27-tennis-regions/ . Spring team draw: https://www.misshsaa.com/2026/11/11/2026-27-class-i-4a-team-tennis-bracket/ .

item.title: Prentiss County court records go offline Dec. 23. Here is how to reach the local clerks.
item.description: People who need a Prentiss County chancery or circuit court document over the Christmas holidays have until 5 p.m. Central Wednesday, Dec. 23, to retrieve it through Mississippi Electronic Courts. The state judiciary’s notice says both the online public search and the public terminals in the courthouse will be unavailable. Clerks will also lose access to the electronic records. The First Circuit Court lists the Prentiss County Courthouse at 101 North Main Street in Booneville. Its circuit clerk can be reached at 662-728-4611. The state directory lists 662-728-8151 for the Prentiss County chancery clerk. The statewide order provides for paper filing at the appropriate clerk’s counter during regular business hours. The state identifies Monday, Dec. 28, through Thursday, Dec. 31, as the four business days affected. Clerks will stamp documents when they receive them. That date stays with the filing when the document is entered electronically later. The state needs the outage to move cases, files and users as new judicial districts take effect Jan. 1. Electronic service is scheduled to return at 8 a.m. Central Monday, Jan. 4, 2027. The Administrative Office of Courts will announce restoration at mec.ms.gov. The state appellate courts retain electronic filing. State notice: https://www.harrisoncountymschanceryclerk.gov/downloads/news/MEC%20Shutdown%20Notice%2011122026.pdf . State Supreme Court order: https://www.harrisoncountymschanceryclerk.gov/downloads/news/MSSC%20ADMINISTRATIVE%20ORDER%20-%202026-AD-00001-SCT%20-%20JUDICIAL%20REDISTRICTING.pdf . Local clerk directory: https://www.sos.ms.gov/sites/default/files/publications/County%20Offices%20and%20Directory_2026.pdf . County courthouse address: https://www.firstcircuitcourt.ms.gov/courthouse-locations . The state’s notice describes what happens to filings on either side of the shutdown. Items sent electronically before the system goes offline will move with the records. During the outage, a new case can still start at the clerk’s counter. The clerk accepts the complaint and fee, and the system assigns a case number when the paper record is entered. The date stamped on the complaint determines the filing year. A complaint received on Dec. 28 still receives a 2026 case number after staff enter it in January. The same state notice says staff may issue summonses and subpoenas on paper and upload copies later. Clerks have instructions to enter orders signed during the outage and urgent filings first when electronic service resumes, followed by new cases and then other documents in the order received. The public may therefore see entries appear after the system returns even though the clerk accepted the documents earlier. The Administrative Office of Courts lists the MEC Help Desk at 601-576-4650 for questions about electronic service. The county clerks are the local contacts for their own offices and filings.
item.source: Mississippi Administrative Office of Courts, Mississippi Supreme Court and Mississippi Secretary of State

item.title: Northeast students return from Thanksgiving for four days before seated classes end
item.description: At Northeast Mississippi Community College in Booneville, full-term seated classes end Thursday, Dec. 3. Thanksgiving closure runs through Friday, Nov. 27. That leaves Monday through Thursday of the following week before the final regular day. Fall final exams run Monday, Dec. 7, through Thursday, Dec. 10. The college also lists fall commencement on Thursday, Dec. 10. The exam schedule groups students by their usual class day and period. For example, a class that meets Monday and Wednesday at 8 a.m. takes its exam Monday, Dec. 7, at 8 a.m. A class that meets Tuesday and Thursday at 8 a.m. takes its exam at 8 a.m. Tuesday, Dec. 8. Classes that usually start at 9:25 a.m. sit for an 8 a.m. exam Wednesday or Thursday, depending on which pair of days they meet. The other daytime exam blocks start at 10:30 a.m. and 1 p.m. Evening college exams meet on the class’s regular night beginning Dec. 7. Northeast says it has no makeup days for finals and directs students who miss an exam to contact the instructor immediately. For students who need an office after exams, the calendar lists administrative offices open Dec. 14–17 before winter closure starts Dec. 18. Official fall exam timetable: https://catalog.nemcc.edu/general-information/exam-schedule.html . Academic calendar: https://catalog.nemcc.edu/general-information/calendar.html . The college timetable gives six daytime class periods. Students who normally meet at 10:50 a.m. on Monday and Wednesday take their exam Monday at 10:30 a.m.; the Tuesday and Thursday group with that same usual start time takes it Tuesday at 10:30 a.m. Classes that normally start at 12:45 p.m. take their exams at 10:30 a.m. Wednesday for the Monday/Wednesday section or Thursday for the Tuesday/Thursday section. The last exam block each day begins at 1 p.m. Classes that usually meet at 2:10 p.m. take it Monday or Tuesday. Those that usually meet at 3:30 p.m. take it Wednesday or Thursday. Students should select their class column from the Fall 2026 table; a separate Spring 2027 timetable appears below it on the same page. The December graduation ceremony falls on the final exam day. For students doing spring registration, offices reopen Monday, Jan. 4. The academic calendar lists extended registration hours at all campuses through 3 p.m. Friday, Jan. 8, before full-term seated classes begin Monday, Jan. 11.
item.source: Northeast Mississippi Community College academic calendar and final exam schedule

item.title: Booneville’s Hailee Lawless takes 540-assist season into North all-star selection
item.description: The final two matches tell different stories about those 38 assists. Booneville had to win the second set by two points to sweep Choctaw County. The recorded scores were 25–17, 25–23 and 25–21. Against Belmont the Blue Devils led two sets to one after taking the first 25–18 and the third 25–19. They lost the second set 25–23. Both remaining sets were decided by two points. Belmont took the fourth 27–25 and the fifth 15–13. Thus Lawless had 20 assists on a night when Booneville was two points from winning the fourth set at 25–25 and played a fifth set. These box scores are the source for the individual set margins. Choctaw County playoff match: https://www.maxpreps.com/ms/volleyball/match/booneville-vs-choctaw-county-ackerman/10-6-2026/?c=ca5f954e-9ea8-43b5-9530-6d76cebb0bbf . Belmont playoff match: https://www.maxpreps.com/ms/volleyball/match/belmont-vs-booneville/10-8-2026/?c=fbe9b7e8-4f7f-475d-aaf0-50b960551b20 . Booneville junior Hailee Lawless recorded 46 assists in the Blue Devils’ three playoff matches this fall. She is the only Booneville player listed on the Mississippi Association of Coaches’ 15-player North roster for next summer’s all-star game. The association gives October 28 as the selection date. This is a look at how Lawless finished her season and the event that awaits her in 2027. The official North roster image lists her as number 3, Booneville, with Adam Mauney as her high school coach. The North team coaches named at the bottom of the official roster are Lewisburg’s Amy Hendrichovsky and New Albany’s Ashley Connolly. Kossuth’s Willow Hatcher also appears on the North roster. Kossuth was Booneville’s final regular-season opponent. Across 112 sets Booneville credited Lawless with 540 assists, 125 serving aces, 259 digs and 120 kills in its records on MaxPreps. She averaged 4.8 assists a set. Her school roster identifies her as a junior who plays setter and outside hitter. Booneville finished 24–13 overall and 5–3 in its district. Her game log and the school’s results track three October tournament matches. Lawless started the postseason with eight assists in three sets in an October 3 sweep of O’Bannon. In another three-set win against Choctaw County on October 6, she recorded 18 assists. Her highest total of those three matches was 20 in a five-set October 8 loss to Belmont. She had also recorded 31 assists in five sets of the September 29 win over Hickory Flat. The 2027 North–South all-star event is scheduled for Wednesday, July 14 at 6 p.m. at Brandon High School in Brandon. Players report Tuesday, July 13. The association lists $10 admission and accepts MAC cards. Fans can purchase tickets on GoFan or at the gate. Source for selection and coaching assignments: https://www.mscoaches.com/sports/volleyball/rosters/north-team . Source for date, admission and reporting time frame: https://www.mscoaches.com/sports/volleyball . Game-by-game and full-season individual results: https://www.maxpreps.com/ms/booneville/booneville-blue-devils/athletes/hailee-lawless/?careerid=spb3mp5do8btd . Team match records: https://www.maxpreps.com/ms/booneville/booneville-blue-devils/volleyball/ .

item.title: Northeast schedules two December entrance ACT sessions in Booneville
item.description: Northeast distinguishes its entrance test from ACT preparation. The Office of Continuing Education lists a separate $45 workshop at 303 Holliday Hall on the Booneville campus. It covers skills analysis, test-taking tips and exam strategies. That is a preparation service, with its own registration and fee. The December examinations themselves take place in Wright Hall and cost $75 each. Continuing Education lists 662-720-7296 for workshop questions. The college lists a separate student identification form for applicants who lack an acceptable photo ID. Review that form before testing. The admissions testing office says a reminder email is sent the day before the scheduled test. For those choosing a later test date, the next two Booneville sessions after December are Friday, January 22, and Friday, January 29, 2027, both at 8 a.m.; the same 60-day interval between attempts applies. No additional workshop or national test date is being announced here. Official preparation program: https://www.nemcc.edu/continuinged/act/index.html . Identification form linked by the college: https://www.act.org/content/dam/act/unsecured/documents/Identification-Letter-Form.pdf . Northeast Mississippi Community College lists two December 2026 Booneville sessions for its on-campus Residual ACT. Both begin at 8 a.m. in Wright Hall, Friday, December 4, and Wednesday, December 16. Each session is limited to 20 students, and Northeast links a registration form from its testing page. The college advises registrants to check the page the day before for changes. No seat availability has been verified. The college charges $75, payable by cash, check or money order made payable to NEMCC. Bring current photo ID, pencils and a calculator. A college admission application must be on file or completed before testing. Late arrivals cannot enter. Allow about four hours. A student must wait 60 days between attempts, which rules out using the December 16 session to retake a December 4 test. The score is for admission to Northeast only. It cannot transfer to a four-year college or be used for the Mississippi Tuition Assistance Grant (MTAG). The national ACT is a different test. Counseling services lists Erica Miller at 662-720-7315. Testing dates, rules and registration: https://www.nemcc.edu/success-center/counseling-services/act/index.html . Registration link from the college: https://forms.office.com/r/azX2jWTr0P .

item.title: Severe drought covers 46.6% of Prentiss County for second week
item.description: A separate federal notice gives the new weekly drought reading practical significance for farms in Prentiss County. On November 23 USDA listed Prentiss among the contiguous Mississippi counties eligible under fast-track drought designation S6465. The six primary counties are Chickasaw, Clay, Lee, Monroe, Pontotoc and Union. Prentiss is a neighboring county in the designation. The deadline for an emergency farm loan under this designation is July 6, 2027. USDA says producers should contact their local Farm Service Agency office about filing a notice of loss. Farm losses and available collateral and repayment capacity are reviewed individually. The agency lists equipment or livestock replacement, reorganization of a farm operation and refinancing certain debts as possible uses. County eligibility does not automatically qualify an individual farm or promise a payment. The November 23 notice and the independent November 24 land-area figures measure different things. Producers can look up their own service center at https://www.farmers.gov/working-with-us/service-center-locator . USDA designation, eligible counties and deadline: https://www.fsa.usda.gov/news-events/news/11-23-2026/usda-designates-six-mississippi-counties-natural-disaster-areas . The November 24 county table puts 46.60% of Prentiss County in severe drought and 53.40% in moderate drought. All of the county, which includes Booneville, was at least moderately dry. None reached extreme or exceptional drought. On November 10, the entire county was in the moderate category. The severe share rose from zero to 46.60% on November 17 and stayed there in the November 24 assessment. The percentages are shares of land area. Categories in the U.S. Drought Monitor table are cumulative; the more severe categories are included in the less severe ones. The national map is dated Tuesday, November 24, before Wednesday’s weather. The map does not measure subsequent rainfall. Statewide, extreme drought or worse covered 66.91% of Mississippi on November 24, up from 53.56% the week before. Sources: https://usdmdataservices.unl.edu/api/CountyStatistics/GetDroughtSeverityStatisticsByAreaPercent?aoi=28117&startdate=11/10/2026&enddate=11/24/2026&statisticsType=1 (county area percentages for November 10, 17 and 24); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/data/png/20261124/20261124_ms_text.png (dated state map and statewide comparison).

item.title: Gilbert’s late layups help Northeast men finish 84–80 comeback after women win 68–58
item.description: Tuesday’s games in Booneville completed the home-and-away series with Arkansas State Mid-South for both Northeast teams. The men’s team previewed the rematch as its chance to sweep the Greyhounds after a 91–64 win at West Memphis on November 10. The Lady Tigers won 70–58 there the same night. The return games gave both Northeast teams season sweeps. The men came in 7–2 after two wins at a tournament in Georgia and left 8–2 with a fourth consecutive victory. The women came in 6–1 after beating Coastal Alabama–North and left 7–1 with their seventh win in a row. Before the season, women’s coach Brian Middleton said he chose an early schedule that would challenge his team. The women’s conference opener is January 11 at Holmes. The men next play at Itawamba on December 1 at 6 p.m. The women next host Walters State on December 3 at 5:30 p.m. Both times are Central. Northeast Mississippi Community College hosted Arkansas State Mid-South for a women’s and men’s varsity basketball doubleheader in Booneville on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. The two schools played each other in both games. The Lady Tigers won the opener 68–58 and the Northeast men won the second game 84–80. The original game books contain the official period scores, substitutions, team and individual statistics and every scoring play. In the men’s game Northeast trailed 46–34 at halftime and fell behind by 17 with 11:43 left in the second half. The Tigers scored 50 points in the second half while holding the visitors to 34. Arkansas State Mid-South’s Tyler McCrary made a three-pointer with 2:18 left to put the visitors in front 79–77. Northeast’s Issac Gilbert tied it on a layup with 1:56 to play. Gilbert scored on another layup at 1:18 and made the accompanying free throw for an 82–79 lead. TJ Warren and Jalen Chandler each made a free throw in the final 41 seconds. The lead reached four when Chandler made his free throw with nine seconds to play. Gilbert finished with 25 points and 11 rebounds, seven on the offensive end. Chandler finished with 19 points, seven rebounds and six assists. Warren had 12 points and five assists. The Tigers led 48–32 on points in the paint and 29–17 on second-chance points. DeAngelo Craig had 23 points for the visitors and Kaleel Sutton-White scored 22. In the women’s opener, Northeast trailed 19–18 after the first quarter, then led 32–28 at halftime and 49–41 after three quarters. Jordyn Crumedy scored 12 off the bench, Lauren Norwood had 11 points and five assists, and Kazli Timbes scored 10. Ashia Williams grabbed 10 rebounds and blocked four shots in 14 minutes off the bench. Her layup with 2:58 left put the Lady Tigers up 68–52. Shatayla Boyland scored the last six points for Arkansas State Mid-South and finished with 25. Northeast won the rebounding comparison 53–36. Both official box scores are required to distinguish the scores and players. item.title: Prentiss County unemployment rises to 3.7% in October
item.description: Prentiss County, Mississippi, including Booneville. The October 2026 preliminary residence-based estimates in the Mississippi Department of Employment Security report put the local unemployment rate at 3.7% in October after a revised 3.2% in September. The August rate was 3.1%. The department counts 9,823 county residents in the October civilian labor force. Of them 9,459 were employed and 364 were unemployed. In September the labor force numbered 9,918, with 9,602 employed and 316 unemployed. The unemployed total rose by 48 residents. The employed count fell by 143. The change in the civilian labor force was -95 people. The survey describes people age 16 and older by where they live. A resident who commutes outside the county remains part of the county residence-based estimates. These counts should not be described as employers adding or eliminating positions. The number unemployed and the number employed together equal the civilian labor force in each month. The comparable Mississippi rate was 3.6%, based on 45,914 unemployed and 1,214,626 employed residents in a civilian labor force of 1,260,540. Both state and county figures in this comparison are unadjusted for seasonal changes. A separate county table in the same release lists 27 initial unemployment insurance claims and 119 continued claims in October compared with 16 initial and 123 continued claims in September. Insurance claims are an administrative measure. They should not be added together or treated as the number of unemployed residents. September is revised and October is preliminary. The tables do not establish what caused any change. The department’s county series gives these monthly rates earlier in 2026: June at 3.9%, July at 3.7%, August at 3.1%, September at 3.2%, October at 3.7%. Source documents: https://mdes.ms.gov/media/23357/labormarketdata.pdf (labor force estimates and county unemployment insurance claims); https://mdes.ms.gov/media/8735/urate.pdf (county monthly unemployment series); https://mdes.ms.gov/media/8654/uratesmapbw.pdf (October county unemployment rate map). The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics describes the purpose of these local-area estimates. State and local governments use them to plan budgets and determine where employment and training services are needed. Federal programs use them when allocating funds and determining eligibility. The estimates measure local economic conditions each month. The Bureau describes these general uses and does not identify a funding or service change specific to Prentiss County. Federal program overview: https://www.bls.gov/lau/lauov.htm.

item.title: Booneville forecast puts heaviest Thanksgiving travel rain Wednesday, with a low of 26 Thursday night
item.description: The National Weather Service Memphis forecast office issued its Monday evening area forecast discussion at 5:50 p.m. Central November 23, 2026. The following local forecast is for the city of Booneville, Prentiss County, Mississippi. The NWS point service identifies the grid as MEG 97,47 at the center of Booneville. These are forecast conditions in Central time, not observations. For travelers leaving before Thanksgiving, Tuesday afternoon is the drier window in the Booneville point forecast. Rain becomes likely after midnight Tuesday night, with the highest probabilities on Wednesday. The Wednesday daytime local forecast calls for three quarters of an inch to one inch of rain. The Wednesday night local forecast calls for an additional one quarter to one half inch. Rainfall totals are possible amounts for those separate forecast periods, not guaranteed totals. The hourly forecast pinpoints the overnight change for drivers. Tuesday, November 24 at 6 PM Central in Booneville: 50 degrees Fahrenheit and a 1 percent chance of precipitation. Tuesday, November 24 at 10 PM Central in Booneville: 45 degrees Fahrenheit and a 2 percent chance of precipitation. Wednesday, November 25 at 2 AM Central in Booneville: 44 degrees Fahrenheit and a 38 percent chance of precipitation. Wednesday, November 25 at 6 AM Central in Booneville: 44 degrees Fahrenheit and a 94 percent chance of precipitation. Tuesday, 2026-11-24: Mostly sunny. High near 56, with temperatures falling to around 52 in the afternoon. North northeast wind 10 to 15 mph. Tuesday Night, 2026-11-24: Rain likely after midnight. Mostly cloudy, with a low around 41. North northeast wind 5 to 10 mph. Chance of precipitation is 60%. New rainfall amounts less than a tenth of an inch possible. Wednesday, 2026-11-25: Rain. Cloudy. High near 53, with temperatures falling to around 49 in the afternoon. North northeast wind 5 to 10 mph. Chance of precipitation is 100%. New rainfall amounts between three quarters and one inch possible. Wednesday Night, 2026-11-25: Rain likely. Mostly cloudy, with a low around 36. North northwest wind 5 to 10 mph. Chance of precipitation is 70%. New rainfall amounts between a quarter and half of an inch possible. Thanksgiving Day, 2026-11-26: Partly sunny. High near 48, with temperatures falling to around 44 in the afternoon. West northwest wind around 15 mph. Thursday Night, 2026-11-26: A slight chance of rain showers before midnight. Mostly clear, with a low around 26. West wind 5 to 15 mph. Chance of precipitation is 20%. Friday, 2026-11-27: Sunny, with a high near 55. West wind 5 to 10 mph. Friday Night, 2026-11-27: Mostly clear, with a low around 29. The area discussion describes a slow-moving system bringing rain east of Memphis Wednesday. Its broader outlook says rain may linger on Thanksgiving mainly along and north of Interstate 40. Use the Booneville point forecast for local conditions. item.title: Booneville High, New Site, Wheeler and the Prentiss County career center appear on TVA’s STEM award roster
item.description: Booneville High School — Prentiss County Electric Power Association. New Site High School — Prentiss County Electric Power Association. Prentiss County Career and Technology Center — Prentiss County Electric Power Association. Wheeler Attendance Center — Prentiss County Electric Power Association. TVA's spreadsheet lists four entries under Prentiss County Electric Power Association. They represent two public school districts. The Booneville School District school directory identifies Booneville High School. The Prentiss County School District separately identifies New Site High School, Wheeler Attendance Center and the district's career and technical center. The career center gives its Booneville address as 302 W. George E. Allen Drive. Its regular course offerings include computer science and engineering, welding, construction and carpentry, auto service technology, and agriculture and natural resources. The course list describes the center. The award spreadsheet has three columns, district, power company and school, with no project descriptions or amounts for individual recipients. The four entries therefore establish the identity of each recipient. No particular course, project or expenditure can be attributed to these awards from those records. The Tennessee Valley Authority and Bicentennial Volunteers, Inc., its retiree organization, announced the regional awards on November 23, 2026. The 2026–27 list contains 334 school entries across the region, 36 in TVA's Mississippi district. The program awards $1.5 million regionwide and TVA estimates about 96,000 students will benefit across the region. The $5,000 figure is an upper limit for an individual award. It is not the amount awarded to a named school. Eligible schools receive electricity through a local power company served by TVA. The competitive process gives preference to proposals dealing with the environment, energy, economic development or solving community problems. The Tennessee STEM Innovation Network is a program partner and Battelle manages the network. TVA says that since 2018 the partners have provided more than $10.5 million through these awards, supporting more than 940,000 students across the region. Primary award announcement: https://www.tva.com/the-powerhouse/stories/tva-awards--1.5-million-to-support-stem-education-across-the-valley_edu Award program and full recipient list: https://www.tva.com/learn/stem-awards Official workbook: https://tva-azr-eastus-cdn-ep-tvawcm-prd.azureedge.net/cdn-tvawcma/docs/default-source/tva-stem/2026--2027-tva-stem-award.xlsx?sfvrsn=87e985be_1 School district sources: https://www.boonevilleschools.org/, https://www.prentisscountyschools.com/, https://www.prentisscountyctc.com/ TVA's previous recipient list confirms that the Prentiss County Career and Technology Center also received a STEM award in 2024–25. The earlier Mississippi list also includes Hills Chapel. That is historical context; Hills Chapel is not among the four current entries under the Prentiss County Electric Power Association. The county district's school directory shows how the current recipients differ in the grades they serve. New Site High School serves grades nine through twelve at 1020 Highway 4 East in New Site. Wheeler Attendance Center serves prekindergarten through twelfth grade at 318 County Road 5011 and has a Booneville mailing address. The district lists the career center separately. Previous TVA list: https://www.tva.com/stem/2024-2025-grant-recipients . District directory: https://www.prentisscountyschools.com/our-district/our-schools .
